Application # 22791-T1

SUBSTITUTE NARRATIVE AND PLANS FOR TYPE 1 ZONING AMENDMENT FOR
7756 SOUTH MORGAN ST., CHICAGO

The subject property is currently improved with a 100-year-old church building which has been
vacant for some time. The Applicant intends to rehab the existing building and adaptively reuse it
to establish a Transitional Residence for women and children, with accessory offices. The
Applicant needs a zoning change to a BJ-3 Neighborhood Shopping District, with optional
variation relief for the setbacks and an administrative adjustment to eliminate all parking
requirements for the proposed use at the property, and to comply with the standards and the bulk
requirements of the Ordinance for this adaptive reuse and preservation project - seeking any and
all relief needed or necessary as per Type | Plans attached and as allowed by Code.

Project Zoning Change from an RS3 Residential Single-Unit (Detached
Description: House) District to a B1-3 Neighborhood Shopping District.
Use: Adaptive Reuse of the existing Building to establish a Transitional

Residence with accessory offices.

Lot Area: 80' x 124.45'= 9,956 SF (recorded measurements)

Floor Area Ratio: | 1.7

Floor Area: 16,496 SF (see plans attached)

(Total building area including basement below grade is 22,552 SF)
Density: Not Applicable
Off- Street Parking spaces: 0 (see administrative adjustment request below)

Final for Publication

L Optional Relief for Adjustment and Variation under Section 17-13-0303-D —

a Type 1 map amendment pursuant to Section 17-13-0300, may include relief available
pursuant to Section 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100; in such instances, City Council approval of a
Type-1 application containing said elements shall preclude subsequent review otherwise
required pursuant to Sections 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100, provided that no Type 1
application permits issued may be in violation of Section 17-13-0310:

(A) With this Type 1 Rezoning, the Applicant also seeks relief for Administrative Adjustment
under section 17-13-1003-EE, from the parking requirements as allowed by Section 17-
10-0102-B Transit-Served Locations, to eliminate all parking requirements, as they would
be required by Section 17-10-0207-Q Parking Group Q.

(B) _ Ifdetermined that these bulk regulations are applicable to this project, the Applicant also
seeks relief for variations under section 17-13-1100, from all bulk requirements of Section
17-2-0300 Bulk and Density Standards, including Sections 17-2-0305 Front Setback, 17-
2-0306 Rear Setbacks, |7-2-0307 Rear Yard Open Space, | 7-2-0309 Side Setbacks and
17-2-0311 Building Height.

In support of the above requests, the Applicant states the following:

1. Strict compliance with the regulations and standards of this Zoning Ordinance would create
practical difficulties and hardships for the subject property, since the subject property is
already improved with an existing non-conforming building which was built more than 100
years ago. The Applicant is proposing to preserve, rehab and adaptively reuse the existing
building, as the Ordinance encourages owners to do. Strict compliance would require
demolishing a large portion of the existing nonconforming structures, causing great hardship
for the owner and the applicant.

2. The requested variations are consistent with the stated purpose and intent of this Zoning
Ordinance since this proposed redevelopment and corresponding variations are seeking to
preserve, rehab and adaptively reuse this historic property. The proposed improvements will
bring the existing building into compliance with the current Building and Fire Code. The
proposed rehab is compatible with the existing land use pattern on the subject block, and it
will not increase any of the existing non-conformities. The proposed preservation project will
beautify the streetscape, remove long-time vacancy and most of all will provide much-needed
services for the Community.

3. Evidence of Practical Difficulties or Particular Hardship is as follows:

- The property in question cannot yield a reasonable retum if permitted to be used only in
accordance with the strict standards of this Zoning Ordinance, since without these variations,
majority of the existing structures would have to be demolished instead of rehabbed.

- The practical difficulties and particular hardships are due to unique circumstances and are not
generally applicable to other similarly situated properties. The requested variations are needed
to mitigate the existing nonconforming conditions at the property, so that the existing historic
building is preserved, rehabbed and adaptively reused.

- These variations and administrative adjustment will not alter the essential character of the
neighborhood, since this property was developed more than 100 years ago with these existing
setbacks which have become non-conforming under the current Zoning Ordinance and have
been in existence all these years, without any adverse effect to the character of the
neighborhood. In addition, there are other zoning lots within the neighborhood which also do
not strictly comply with the current bulk requirements or parking regulations.
